claims.claim: A community-compiled 5e writer's guide: 'Write in the present tense', avoiding 'will' for NPC/monster actions ('the golem attacks').
claims.source: Dungeon Master Assistance — D&D 5E Writer's Guide (Ronny, 2015-08-03)
claims.quote: Wherever possible, avoid using the future tense

claims.claim: In 2024 text, Bonus Action, Advantage/Disadvantage, Hit Points, Armor Class, Death Saving Throw, Proficiency Bonus, Challenge Rating and D20 Test are capitalized while ability, action, saving throw, skill, spell and feat stay lowercase; monster-name capitalization is inconsistent.
claims.source: Blog of Holding — Unofficial D&D 2024 Style Guide (Paul Hughes, 2025-01-07)

claims.claim: Justin Alexander: 2024 capitalizes defined terms (Cone, Target) to flag Rules Glossary entries, but definitions then live only in the glossary, scattering the targeting rules across pp. 236–238, 361, 364 and 376.
claims.source: The Alexandrian — D&D 5E 2024: Why Rules Glossaries Kinda Suck (2024-08-28)

claims.claim: 2024 condition text is standardized to mechanical statements — 'Your Speed is 0 and can't increase' replaces 2014's 'can't move' — and 'Utilize', 'Study', 'Influence' and 'D20 Test' become defined capitalized terms.
claims.source: Dungeon Master Assistance — D&D 5.5 PHB Review: Playing the Game and the Rules Glossary (Ronny, 2024-10-01)
claims.quote: Your Speed is 0 and can't increase

claims.feature: teach-first structure and annotated play example (2024)
claims.claim: The 2024 PHB opens with a How to Play chapter and a two-column example of play annotated with the applicable rules; Crawford frames the rewrite as 'teaching you how to play', contrasting 2014 which 'jumps right into character creation'.
claims.source: Wargamer — New DnD Player's Handbook aims to actually teach you the game (2024-06-18)

claims.claim: Idle Cartulary judges the 48-page rules section plus 18-page glossary 'absolutely stellar information design' and 'an incredibly confident book', though terms like Influence action lack definition where used.
claims.source: Idle Cartulary (Playful Void) — I Read The Player's Handbook (2024) (2024-08-31)

claims.claim: Mearls' 2013 Legends & Lore argument, as quoted: feat names like 'Rapid Shot and Precise Shot are abstract things that aren't really clear', whereas describing a fighter as an archer 'makes sense to anyone'; rules are 'a shared language'.
claims.source: Tenkar's Tavern — Mike Mearls' Latest Legends & Lore Column: Where Less is More (2013-03-03)

claims.claim: A 2014 EN World thread infers that 5e designers chose rulings over exact language, which lets them 'use more natural language' — community inference from Mearls' videos, not a designer statement about prose.

5e core-book editor Scott Fitzgerald Gray: mechanics editing needs precision in how a book 'fits in with the game as a whole', narrative editing needs flow and pacing, and prose editing serves 'the emotional language of the game' so readers feel like a character in the world.
claims.source: Shadomain — Tales From the Tavern: Interview with Scott Fitzgerald Gray (2024-03-20)
claims.quote: the emotional language of the game

claims.claim: Perkins says every adventure for a decade had to re-explain doors, so the 2024 DMG codifies them; Wyatt calls re-explaining boxed text in every adventure a 'stupid little thing' the DMG (p. 9) now covers, pending the editing team.
claims.source: Screen Rant — After DM's Guide Preview, I'm Convinced Future D&D Adventures Will Drop These Two Repetitive Features (Ben Brosofsky, 2024-10-29)

claims.claim: Perkins on the 2024 DMG: 'everything in there better be cracking on topic'; the sample adventures use 'tight and short' read-aloud scripts to jog the DM's memory, avoiding his earlier 32-page adventures.
claims.source: Screen Rant — 'Everything In There Better Be Cracking On Topic': D&D Designers Talk The 2024 DMG (Perkins & Wyatt interview, 2024-10-25)

claims.feature: Curse of Strahd vs Storm King's Thunder boxed text
claims.claim: DMDavid observes Perkins boxed every location in Curse of Strahd, even empty rooms, and that his next adventure, Storm King's Thunder, 'omits almost all read-aloud text' — the two extremes of WotC 5e practice.
claims.source: DMDavid — How much description should a dungeon key include? (David Hartlage, 2016-11-21)

claims.claim: Every 2025 MM entry opens with a single characterizing phrase ('tentacled subterranean trapper', 'guardian manifestation of the divine'); lore is 'compact but effective' though 'a little too compact for my taste'; quote boxes appear on some entries.
claims.source: EN World — Monsters & More: An In-Depth Review of the 2025 D&D Monster Manual (Beth Rimmels, 2025-01-28)

claims.claim: TheGamer: 'The flavor has amped up narratively, and the mechanics have followed' (angels wield light, kenku use shadow-magic daggers); there is no lore glossary.

Xanathar's Guide carries 'little notes that run as commentary throughout the book, usually a sort of joke or snipe about the subject matter', continuing the Volo's device but less relevant on a mechanics-heavy book.
claims.source: Skyland Games — Review: Xanathar's Guide to Everything (Scott D, 2017-11-13)
claims.quote: a sort of joke or snipe about the subject matter

verdicts.trueWording: Write in the present tense. Wherever possible, avoid using the future tense
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. Tense section verbatim: 'Write in the present tense. Wherever possible, avoid using the future tense "will" to describe NPC or monster actions. For example, do not say "If the player characters open the door, the golem will attack." Instead say, "If the player characters open the door, the golem attacks."' Every limb supported. Minor framing note: the guide is one blogger's (Ronny's) unofficial compilation updated from his 3.5/4.0 copies, so 'community-compiled' means fan-made rather than crowd-authored.

verdicts.trueWording: Capitalized list includes Bonus Action, D20 Test; not capitalized includes feat
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. All eight capitalized terms appear verbatim in the 'Capitalized:' list (Advantage/Disadvantage, Armor Class, Bonus Action, Challenge Rating, D20 Test, Death Saving Throw, Hit Points, Proficiency Bonus). All six lowercase terms appear verbatim in the 'Not Capitalized:' list (ability, action, saving throw, skill, spell, feat). Monster-name inconsistency verbatim: 'monster name ("skeleton") (or perhaps its "Skeleton", it's inconsistent)'. Claim carried no quote field; every named term is literal.

verdicts.trueWording: 'Cube' is capitalized, which indicates a term in the Rules Glossary
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl; claim carried no quote field, so graded on substance. Capitalization-flags-glossary supported: '"Cube" is capitalized, which indicates a term that's located in the Rules Glossary'. Cone example supported: a Cone area of effect 'will never be explained in the text: It will only be defined in the "Cone [Area of Effect]" section of the Rules Glossary'. Target glossary entry p. 376; Target rules pp. 237-8; Range p. 236; conclusion names the lookup path 'page 376, then page 237, then page 364, and then page 361'. Nuance: p. 236 is the Range rules, not strictly targeting, so the range '236-238' is the claim's own compression.

verdicts.trueWording: Your Speed is 0 and can't increase
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. Quote verbatim: 'Any condition that had "can't move", was changed to "Your Speed is 0 and can't increase."' Standardization further supported by 'can't speak' being consolidated into Incapacitated. INFLUENCE and STUDY each flagged '(This is a new action.)'; UTILIZE 'is a renaming of the old "Use an Object" action'; 'D20 TEST: This is a simple new definition that they have added.' Capitalization of the action names is shown by the page's own usage (e.g. 'now called D20 Tests', 'Heavily Obscured', 'Hide check') and its all-caps headings rather than asserted outright.

verdicts.trueWording: will start by 'teaching you how to play' DnD
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. Both quotes verbatim: 'Crawford states that the new Player's Handbook will start by "teaching you how to play" DnD' and 'The current Player's Handbook jumps right into character creation'. How to Play chapter named ('The art in the How to Play chapter'). Two-column annotation verbatim: 'Text examples use a two-column format, with the left of the page used for a dialogue between players during a game, and rules commentary boxes on the right explaining what rules are in play in the example.' Attribution nuance: 'jumps right into character creation' is the Wargamer writer's own sentence, not a Crawford quote - do not cite it as his words.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the 48-page rules section plus 18-page glossary' - the 18 pages are inside the 48, not additional (29 rules pages + 18-page glossary = 'These 48 pages')
verdicts.trueWording: 29 pages of rules plus an 18-page glossary make 48
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. Both quotations verbatim: 'The organisation and use of the rules glossary is absolutely stellar information design' and 'This is an incredibly confident book.' Influence limb verbatim: 'the Influence action isn't defined in the social interaction section for example'. But the page reads 'It summarises the lot of them in 29 pages... helped in great part by the 18 page rules glossary in Appendix C it depends on. These 48 pages aren't just rules', and later '(compared to 48)' as the 2024 core-rules total - so the claim double-counts the glossary. Second, smaller slippage: 'absolutely stellar information design' is applied specifically to the organisation and use of the rules glossary, not to the 48 pages as a whole.

verdicts.trueWording: D&D is a shared language. The rules serve to make it easier
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl; Tenkar's Tavern post of Sunday, March 3, 2013 blockquoting Mearls' column. Verbatim: 'Rapid Shot and Precise Shot are abstract things that aren't really clear', 'Describing your fighter as an archer, though, makes sense to anyone', 'D&D is a shared language.' Nuance: the page says D&D (not 'rules') is the shared language - the next sentence is 'The rules serve to make it easier to talk about the game'. 'Feat names' is contextual inference; Mearls does not call Rapid Shot/Precise Shot feats in the quoted passage.

verdicts.trueWording: allows them to state things more plainly and use more natural language
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. OP by Thaumaturge, Jun 25, 2014, thread 'Design Philosophy of 5e'. Quote verbatim: 'I think a benefit of this is it allows them to state things more plainly and use more natural language.' Rulings-over-exact-language limb verbatim: 'To let real people make real rulings that impact their own play instead of trying to nail down a specific style of play through exact language.' Community-inference framing correct - the natural-language line is the poster's own 'I think', hung off the Mearls Starter Set Unboxing video (one video, cited at ~46:15/48:00), not a designer statement about prose.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: '5e core-book editor' - the interview never says Gray edited the 5e core rulebooks; it names Secrets of Sarlona (3e Eberron) and Vault of the Dracolich, and 'freelance editing for Wizards'
verdicts.trueWording: Prose editing requires attention to the emotional language of the game
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. The substance of the three-layer answer is verbatim: 'Mechanics in RPGs need a specific amount of precision and clarity, not just within a single book but in terms of how that book fits in with the game as a whole. Narrative within a book needs attention to flow and pacing more than attention to words. Prose editing requires attention to the emotional language of the game and how a book can make the game feel real, so that a player reading an RPG doesn't just feel like a player reading rules - they feel on some level like a character in the world that the game creates.' He names the three layers 'narrative editing, rules editing, and prose editing'. What this page does NOT establish is the credential: no mention of the 5e Player's Handbook, DMG or Monster Manual anywhere in the interview. Cite the credential from a credits page, not from here.

verdicts.trueWording: James Wyatt has his own 'stupid little thing' that's been irking him
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl. Doors limb: 'Having to explain doors in every published adventure has apparently been irking him for the past decade' and the DMG's 'page on doors... a standardized set of information'. Wyatt limb verbatim: 'James Wyatt has his own "stupid little thing" that's been irking him - having to explain what boxed text is in every adventure.' Page 9 limb verbatim: 'explaining how it works on page 9 under a section telling DMs how to describe situations'. Editing-team limb verbatim: 'It's something that has to be hashed out with the editing team first'. Note the Perkins doors line is the interviewer's paraphrase of the interview; his only direct quote there is 'super, super important'.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'read-aloud scripts' - the page says the sample adventures are 'scripts for the DM to just to jog their memory', i.e. DM-facing, not read-aloud/boxed text for players
verdicts.trueWording: scripts for the DM to just to jog their memory
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl (Screen Rant interview, Ben Brosofsky, Oct 25 2024). Perkins verbatim: 'everything in there better be cracking on topic and directed at DMs who are either new or who are looking for ways as experienced DMs to make their games more interesting.' And: 'I remember I was taught that an adventure was like a 32-page publishable thing. And so all of my home adventures I wrote as like 32-page things, fully written out... And so if I had the 2024 DMG, which has sample adventures in it, which are tight and short and really sort of scripts for the DM to just to jog their memory and make sure that they're sort of remembering the pace and flow of the adventure, I could have saved myself a lot of prep time.' 'tight and short' and the jog-the-memory and 32-page limbs are all verbatim; only 'read-aloud' is imported by the claim, and it inverts the audience of the scripts.

verdicts.trueWording: His follow-up, Storm King's Thunder, omits almost all read-aloud text
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl (post by David Hartlage, November 21, 2016, served on the tag archive URL). Verbatim: 'Curse of Strahd includes it for every location.'; 'DMs who dutifully present the box text for all the empty rooms in a place like the Argynvostholt dungeon will bore players.'; 'His follow-up, Storm King's Thunder, omits almost all read-aloud text. Find a happy middle, Chris.' The 'two extremes' framing is the claim's own wording but is carried by 'Find a happy middle' (and a commenter's 'On the other end of the spectrum, I find Storm King's Thunder barren').

verdicts.trueWording: the Couatl is 'guardian manifestation of the divine' and the Roper 'tentacled subterranean trapper'
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl (EN World review by Beth Rimmels / brimmels, Jan 28 2025). Verbatim: 'every entry starts with a single phrase that gives the DM an efficient characterization of the creature. So the Couatl is "guardian manifestation of the divine" and the Roper is a "tentacled subterranean trapper."' Lore limbs verbatim in two places: 'The lore/background material is compact - a little too compact for my taste' and 'Narrative/lore material is compact but effective.' Quote boxes limb verbatim: 'Quote boxes are another way the new MM adds a bit more flavor and insight. Not every entry gets them'.

verdicts.trueWording: The flavor has amped up narratively, and the mechanics have followed
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl (TheGamer, Jerel Levy, Published Jan 28 2025). Verbatim: 'The flavor has amped up narratively, and the mechanics have followed.' Angel example verbatim: 'where an angel might have been wielding a greatsword in the past... it now wields light itself in combat'. Kenku verbatim: 'The Kenku, known for being from the Shadowfell, now have a dagger with shadow magic.' No-lore-glossary limb verbatim: 'Though there is no lore glossary similar to what the Dungeon Master's Guide has'. Claim carried no quote field; the sentence it paraphrases is literal on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: little notes that run as commentary throughout the book, usually a joke
verdicts.note: Raw page read via curl (Skyland Games, Scott D, November 13, 2017). Whole claim verbatim in one sentence pair: 'As with Volo's Guide to Monsters, there are little notes that run as commentary throughout the book, usually a sort of joke or snipe about the subject matter. As the material is largely mechanics and game lore, it's less relevant than with Volo's but still fun.' Every limb - the device, the Volo's lineage, and the reduced relevance on a mechanics-heavy book - is on the page.
